summary: A cardholder makes a modest purchase during the billing cycle, stays under the credit limit, receives a statement, and then pays the full statement balance before the due date. The scenario is designed to show timely satisfaction of the minimum-payment obligation with no late fee and no over-limit fee.
assumptions: The account begins this billing cycle with a zero previous balance and no disputed charges, fees, or prior delinquencies.
The credit limit is $1000.00, so a single $200.00 purchase does not exceed the limit and satisfies the credit-limit promise in clause.4.credit_limits.
The statement closes on 2025-03-31 and shows a New Balance of $200.00; under the contract formula, the minimum payment would be $15.00, but the cardholder instead pays the full $200.00.
The payment is made by an approved standard method and is credited on the date received, with no returned payment or processing delay.
Because payment is made in full on or before the due date, this on-time archetype assumes no late payment fee and no over-credit-limit fee are triggered.
